suggested_patch.rationale: Cap the test surface for a one-line literal assignment; keep one parse-assertion test, one docstring-preservation test, and one diff/commit smoke test.

findings.message: minimum_test_count=12 for a single-line top-level __version__ assignment is extreme test-heaviness. The body of the change is one line of code (literally __version__ = '0.0.1'); demanding 6 unit + 4 integration + 1 property + 1 regression test inflates verification cost far past the change's blast radius. The 'prove the pipeline' smoke is already validated end-to-end by the auto_commit ledger row + py_compile gate; the per-test bookkeeping for 12 distinct assertions adds churn without catching new failure modes. Cut to ~3 tests (assignment present, docstring preserved, dispatch produces a real diff/commit).

suggested_patch.rationale: Keep test budget at most equal to impl budget for a trivial single-line addition; the current 2:1 test:impl ratio is a downstream symptom of the bloated test count.

findings.message: token_budget_ratio allocates 200 test tokens vs 100 implementation tokens (2:1) for a one-line literal. Even with the harness's 'test-heavy' bias, allocating twice the budget to tests for a literal assignment is wasteful and incentivises generating filler test stubs. Tighten to ~1:1 or below once the test count is cut.

suggested_patch.edge_case: The submission MUST end with a single trailing newline (LF); CRLF line endings or a missing terminal newline will produce a noisy diff that may trip the AST merger or pre-commit hooks and obscure the canonical one-line addition.

findings.message: The spec's implementation_notes carefully specifies the verbatim file content including 'the closing newline', but the edge_cases list never warns about line-ending drift (CRLF/CR vs LF) or BOM injection by an editor. Without an explicit edge case, an agent emitting CRLF-encoded content can produce a passing py_compile yet a corrupted diff against the LF-encoded stub. Add an edge case mandating LF line endings, no BOM, and a single terminal newline.

suggested_patch.edge_case: If harness/smoke_target.py already defines __version__ (e.g., from a prior dispatch run that was not reset), the task MUST either no-op gracefully or fail with a clear diagnostic — it MUST NOT introduce a second __version__ assignment or shadow the existing one.

findings.message: The spec assumes the committed stub has no __version__, but does not specify behaviour when the file already defines one (re-run / partial revert / dirty working tree). Without an explicit edge case, a re-dispatch could append a duplicate __version__ assignment, leaving the module syntactically valid but semantically wrong and producing a confusing diff. Add an idempotency edge case.

suggested_patch.detail: Extend the one-liner to also assert the assigned literal equals '0.0.1' (e.g., evaluate the constant and compare), not merely that an assignment to __version__ exists. As written, __version__ = '999.999.999' or __version__ = None would still satisfy the gate.

findings.message: The verification_command only checks for the existence of a top-level Assign to a Name 'id' == '__version__'; it never inspects the assigned value. The spec mandates the literal string '0.0.1' (edge_cases bullet 4), so an agent emitting __version__ = '' or __version__ = '0.0.2' would pass the gate but violate the spec. Strengthen the AST check to assert the assignment's value is a Constant equal to '0.0.1'.
